links.comparator_used: AI examination alone and dermatologist screening alone
links.outcome: Patients' subjective safety score (0-10) and screening preference after augmented intelligence versus AI alone or dermatologist alone
links.effect: mSSS 9.5 (AuI) vs 7.7 (AI), p < 0.0001; 9.5 vs 9.1 (dermatologist alone), p = 0.001. 83.4% of patients preferred AuI-based screening over AI or dermatologist alone (n = 199).
links.tradeoff: Dermatologists still relied largely on their own judgement: in divergent risk assessments only 1.5% (3/205) trusted a benign CNN classification over their own malignancy suspicion. Experts (20.9%) found AI less helpful to their clinical work than beginners (61.8%).
links.quote: Regarding SSS, AuI induced a significantly higher feeling of safety than AI (mean-SSS (mSSS): 9.5 vs. 7.7, p < 0.0001) or dermatologist screening alone (mSSS: 9.5 vs. 9.1, p = 0.001).

design_hint: augmented intelligence (clinician review combined with AI output) for melanoma screening
